subject: Dedicated capacity options and ramp plan for AuroraMed POC
messages:
From: Emma Wong <emma.wong@auroramed.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity proposal request — AuroraMed POC

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the AuroraMed team is excited to move quickly on a two-month POC for chart summarization and triage. Before we kick off, procurement asked for a written proposal that outlines dedicated capacity options, minimum reservation requirements, and an expected ramp schedule so they can budget. High-level numbers from our side:

- Peak inference: ~1,200 concurrent requests during clinical hours (typical 2–4s responses)
- Monthly tokens: ~650M generated tokens (estimate; bursty during day)
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 350ms for short prompts, 99th <= 600ms for longer sequences
- Start date target: 2028-04-01

Can you send a short set of options (cluster sizes, min GPUs, ramp, pricing tiers) plus any recommended buffer strategy for burstiness? Also include whether prewarming or warm standby is recommended for first-week traffic. We will need SOC 2 evidence and a mutual action plan for timelines so procurement can sign off.

Best,
Emma

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>

Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Capacity proposal request — AuroraMed POC

Hi Emma — great to hear the team is ready to proceed. Attached is a concise options package (auroramed-dedicated-options.pdf) and a draft mutual action plan (AM-POC-mutual-action-plan.xlsx). Summary below — I included conservative buffer recommendations and a phased ramp to control spend while protecting latency.

Proposal (three options):

1) Starter Reserve — low-touch POC
- Cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum reservation: 4 GPUs reserved (50% min)
- Ramp: 2-week prewarm + 4-week scale to 8 GPUs (increase by 2 GPUs/week)
- Use-case: cost-sensitive evaluation, non-critical volumes
- Price tier: on-demand blended with small monthly commit

2) Balanced Reserve — standard POC throughput
- Cluster: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs
- Minimum reservation: 12 GPUs (baseline for sustained traffic)
- Ramp: 1-week canary (2 GPUs), 3-week scale to 32 GPUs (doubling cadence then linear add)
- Buffering: 20% headroom above expected sustained peak for batching variance
- Price tier: monthly reserved units with burst credits to shared pool

3) High-Availability Reserve — near-production
- Cluster: 80 x A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool)
- Minimum reservation: 40 GPUs
- Ramp: phased 6-month ramp (monthly staged increases + automated canary windows)
- Buffering: 25% baseline + automated surge routing to verified quantized model variant if capacity saturated
- Price tier: annual commitment with SLA and priority capacity

Operational notes and buffering rationale:
- Minimum reservation guidance: we recommend reserving ~20–30% of peak sustained GPU need as a baseline for smaller – mid POCs. For more predictable latency, we model a minimum of ~12 GPUs for your expected sustained workload in the Balanced scenario. This prevents long cold-start tails and ensures stable batching efficiency.
- Buffering strategy: combine a small reserved buffer (20%) with prewarmed standby nodes for the first 48–72 hours of go-live, and automated burst into Redwood shared pool for short spikes. Where latency is critical, enable prewarming + reduced-precision model fallback to preserve 95/99p SLOs if capacity is exceeded.
- Canary & acceptance: propose a 7-day canary with clear success metrics (latency, error rate, tokens/day). We’ll include an automated rollback if 95p latency exceeds target for >10% of requests.
- Cost control: include a monthly ramp cap to gate each scale step (ops approval triggers) to avoid unexpected invoices.
Attachments: auroramed-dedicated-options.pdf, AM-POC-mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Confirm which option matches procurement’s risk tolerance.
2) We’ll convert the selected option into a draft SOW + DocuSign link and include SOC 2 evidence.
3) Align on go-live date and canary windows.

Happy to jump on a 30-min call this afternoon if useful.
Thanks,
Stephanie Nguyen

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Mar 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity proposal request — Capacity guardrails and recommended minimum

Stephanie — quick internal sync notes before you finalize the SOW to Emma:

- Minimum reservation calc: rather than a flat percent, compute min reservation as max(12 GPUs, 25% of modeled peak sustained). For AuroraMed numbers that gives us 12 GPUs floor (covers batching efficiency) but still allows larger deals to scale min up automatically.
- Include explicit model fallback in the SOW: when burst > reserved+buffer for >120s, route to 8-bit quantized variant (controlled via routing policy) and add a notice to the client dashboard. This keeps the product usable while protecting cost/SLA.
- Canary proposal: 3-step canary (smoke -> 24h perf -> 7d stability). For each step add pass/fail criteria tied to latency percentiles and error rates.
- Ramp cap: set a monthly GPU add cap (e.g., +20 GPUs/month) unless a spend override is accepted by procurement. This avoids runaway scale during POC.
- Security ask: Emma requested SOC 2; attach pointer to hosted SOC 2 report and propose a brief compliance call with security in week 0.

Also recommend we offer an optional short-term surge credit (one-off 10% free burst) to smooth first-week load — useful as a good-faith gesture in the SOW.

I'll review the pricing page numbers with finance and send the finalized tier numbers by EOD.
—Rafael
VP Sales, Redwood Inference

Thanks — this is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement and engineering: 

1) Can you confirm the recommended "min reservation" in the Balanced option will meet our latency SLOs (95p <= 350ms) for typical 256-token prompts? If not, what delta in GPU count would you estimate?
2) For the burst path: does Redwood require AuroraMed to have any extra reserved capacity to use the shared pool, or can we rely on burst credits in the month? We want a clear picture of when we'll see degraded output (quantized fallback) vs. full model.
3) Please send SOC 2 summary and a short list of artifacts we need to provide for a security review.
4) Procurement prefers the 3-step canary but asks that the mutual action plan explicitly states acceptance criteria and a sign-off owner at AuroraMed. We'll fill in names once we have the doc.

If you can respond to 1–3 today, procurement will slot a quick internal review and aim to return a signed SOW by next week. Deal id for our tracking: AM-2028-042.

Emma
